summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of recurrent cellulitis, venous stasis ulcers, chronic pancreatitis, and asthma was admitted for worsening cellulitis of the left lower leg that failed outpatient treatment with minocycline. She presented with spreading erythema, fever, chills, and burning pain, and was started on IV vancomycin in the emergency department. During her two-day hospitalization, her infection improved clinically and her white blood cell count normalized. A chest X-ray showed no acute findings despite her cough and sputum, consistent with an upper respiratory infection. A lower extremity ultrasound ruled out DVT. She was discharged on oral minocycline for a 10-day course and instructed to follow up with her primary care provider for ongoing management and blood culture results.
problems: Cellulitis and abscess of leg, except foot
Acute upper respiratory infections of unspecified site
Spinal stenosis, lumbar region, without neurogenic claudication
